info.description:
Open, modular foundation for unique payments flows

# Introduction
This API is documented in **OpenAPI format**.

# Authentication
Formance Stack offers one forms of authentication:
  - OAuth2
OAuth2 - an open protocol to allow secure authorization in a simple
and standard method from web, mobile and desktop applications.

Creates a new ledger with the specified name. Storage is configured at the server level.
Each ledger has its own Raft group for data consistency. Requires `ledger:write` scope.

The ledger name `_` is reserved: all system / non-ledger routes live
under the `/v3/_/…` segment (e.g. `/v3/_/audit-entries`), so a ledger
named `_` would be unreachable over REST. Creating it is rejected with a
validation error. The exact name `_system` is also reserved for system
events and rejected. Other underscore-prefixed names remain valid.

The seven usage-derived counters (`postingCount`, `revertCount`, `numscriptExecutionCount`, `referenceCount`, `ephemeralEvictedCount`, `transientUsedCount`, `volumeCount`) are materialised asynchronously in the serving replica's usagestore and may lag committed state even after the request's ReadIndex barrier. Note: for checkpoint-scoped (historical) reads, only `transactionCount` and `logCount` are checkpoint-consistent; the usage-derived counters (`postingCount`, `revertCount`, `numscriptExecutionCount`, `referenceCount`, `ephemeralEvictedCount`, `transientUsedCount`, `volumeCount`) are sourced from the live usagestore projection, which is not checkpoint-aware, and are returned as `0` at a checkpoint rather than a live value — treat `0` on a checkpoint read as "not available at this checkpoint".

get.description:
Lists audit trail entries (one per proposal, success or failure) across
the whole bucket, paged by audit sequence (ascending unless
`reverse=true`). Audit reads are
not ledger-scoped in the path — a single proposal can touch several
ledgers — so ledger scope, outcome and other dimensions are expressed
through the `filter` query parameter.

This endpoint always performs a live read and does not expose pinned
checkpoint reads. Filters containing indexed audit conditions wait for
the audit projection to certify the request's fixed main-store horizon;
matching entries are loaded from that same main snapshot. Unfiltered
reads and sequence-only bounds scan the audit zone directly without
waiting for the audit projection.

Requires `ledger:ReadAudit` scope.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description:
A filter, decoded by the same shared dual-format decoder every list
endpoint uses (see the `ListFilter` parameter), restricted to bare
audit fields (`outcome`, `ledger`, `seq`, `proposal_id`,
`timestamp`, `log_seq`, `caller_subject`, `order_type`,
`idempotency_key`). These are
written without any prefix and are resolved against the audit query
target (EN-1549 — this replaced the old `audit[...]` namespaced
syntax; it is a breaking change with no backward compatibility):
  - `outcome == failure`
  - `ledger == main`
  - `order_type in (create_transaction, revert_transaction)`
  - `seq between 1000 and 2000`
  - `timestamp >= "2023-11-14T22:13:20Z"`
  - `idempotency_key == "retry-123"`
  - `idempotency_key ^= "import-2026-"`
Supported fields: `seq`, `proposal_id`, `log_seq` (numeric);
`timestamp` (RFC3339 or unix microseconds); `outcome`
(success|failure), `ledger`, `caller_subject`, `order_type`,
`idempotency_key` (string; `idempotency_key` also supports prefix
matching with `^=`; a reused key returns every historical audit
entry; bare alphanumeric values are accepted unquoted, while values
containing `-`, `:`, spaces, or other non-identifier characters
must be single- or double-quoted; keys containing both `"` and `'`
cannot be expressed in the textual DSL: use the structured form for
exact and `in` lookups (`{"$match":{"idempotency_key":"…"}}`, an
`$or` of such leaves) and the gRPC API directly
(`AuditCondition.string_prefix`) for prefix lookups). Bare audit fields are resolved against the audit query
target: `timestamp` and `ledger` collide with the transaction
`timestamp` field and the top-level `ledger` condition, so on the
audit target they resolve to the audit condition (and only there —
hence audit fields are valid on this endpoint only). The structured
JSON form uses the same bare field names, resolved against the
audit target the same way: `{"$match":{"outcome":"failure"}}`,
`{"$gte":{"seq":1000}}`, `{"$match":{"idempotency_key":"retry-123"}}`.
Parameters (`{"$param": …}`) are rejected on audit fields, and the
`idempotency_key ^=` prefix match has no structured form (the JSON
DSL has no prefix operator).

Signed requests use `application/json` (including MIME parameters) with
`request` and standard-base64 `payload`. Either signing header, even if
empty, selects this wrapper; with neither header present, the ordinary REST body applies.
Runtime headers choose the representation from the documented anyOf.
The signed protobuf batch must
equal the route/body/Idempotency-Key-derived batch in full. Supply exactly
one nonempty Formance-Signing-Key-Id and Formance-Signature header; the
latter is a standard-base64 Ed25519 signature of 64 decoded bytes. Missing,
empty or repeated signing headers, invalid base64 and wrong signature
length return 400. Signing headers with a non-JSON or missing content type return 415.

signatures. Malformed signed envelopes return 400. The complete

get.description:
Lists transactions for a specific ledger. The default order is
newest-first (descending transaction id); pass `reverse=true` to
get oldest-first (ascending). Supports cursor pagination (`pageSize`,
`cursor`), an optional date range (`startDate`/`endDate`),
and the generic `filter` parameter (e.g. reference selection via
`filter={"$match":{"reference":"..."}}`, URL-encoded). Requires
`ledger:ReadTransaction` scope.

This is a live read, linearizable by default. `X-Consistency: stale`
reads the receiving node's local state, which may lag the leader. Every
projection used by the filter is automatically aligned. Unlike the
gRPC API, it does not accept the `checkpointId` option to pin the read
to a specific historical snapshot — use gRPC for checkpoint-pinned
reads. (Tracked follow-up, same carve-out as the audit reads.)

post.description:
Execute multiple operations (create transactions, add metadata,
revert transactions, delete metadata) in a single request. Requires
`ledger:write` scope.

With `atomic=true`, all elements target the URL's ledger and are
submitted as one batch. `Idempotency-Key` identifies that whole batch;
per-element `ik` values are ignored. With `atomic=false`
(default), each element is submitted separately under its own
`ik`; the header is ignored.

`continueOnFailure` controls sequential continuation and business-error
status rollup. It does not allow partial application of an atomic
batch. Non-atomic failures can follow already committed elements:
inspect every result and preserve the original identities when retrying.
A timeout or infrastructure failure does not prove that work was not
committed. This contract does not enable automatic SDK retries.

The response status is decided in three tiers:

1. **Request-level failures** (before per-element processing):
   malformed body → `400`, missing/insufficient scope → `401` or
   `403`, too many elements → `413`. Exceeding the byte limit while
   decoding the body currently returns `400`.
   Returned unconditionally, `continueOnFailure` does not apply.
2. **Infrastructure failures during processing** (transport
   timeout, cache-horizon exceeded, storage error): the overall
   status is `503` for retryable failures and `500` otherwise,
   regardless of `continueOnFailure`. Callers
   must inspect the element outcomes before deciding what to retry.
3. **Per-element errors during processing**: each element's error
   carries the HTTP status it would surface as a single request
   (via the same mapping `handleError` uses). The top-level
   status is the "worst" of them, with `continueOnFailure`
   applying only to per-element business failures (4xx):
   - Business failures (validation, not-found, conflict,
     precondition — 4xx, except authentication/permission): rolled up per
     `continueOnFailure`. `true` → `200`; `false` (default) →
     the highest 4xx among failing elements (typically `400`).
   - Authentication and permission failures: `401`/`403`, regardless
     of `continueOnFailure`, with all processing outcomes retained.
   - Resource exhaustion (`KindResourceExhausted`, `429`), including
     rate limits and permanent authoritative-sequence exhaustion:
     surface unconditionally as `429`.
   - Retryable infrastructure failures (leader loss,
     cache-horizon exceeded, `KindUnavailable`): surface as
     `503` with `Retry-After: 1`, regardless of
     `continueOnFailure`.
   - Non-retryable infrastructure failures (transport / storage
     errors, `KindInternal`, unclassified): surface as `500`.
   - Aborted elements (`context.Canceled` from the sequential
     runner after a prior failure): contribute nothing — the
     originating error drives the rollup.
Signed requests use `application/json` (including MIME parameters) with
`request` and standard-base64 `payload`. Either signing header, even if
empty, selects this wrapper; with neither header present, the ordinary REST body applies.
Runtime headers choose the representation from the documented anyOf.
The signed protobuf batch must
equal the route/body/Idempotency-Key-derived batch in full. Supply exactly
one nonempty Formance-Signing-Key-Id and Formance-Signature header; the
latter is a standard-base64 Ed25519 signature of 64 decoded bytes. Missing,
empty or repeated signing headers, invalid base64 and wrong signature
length return 400. Signing headers with a non-JSON or missing content type return 415.
Signature enforcement
returns 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED` when required but absent and 403
`PERMISSION_DENIED` for invalid, unknown/revoked-key or mismatched
signatures. Malformed signed envelopes return 400. The complete
wrapper counts toward the 4 MiB body limit. JWT scopes still apply.
Signing requires a nonempty array and `atomic=true` (otherwise 400).
The header key applies; per-element `ik` is ignored. Authentication
and permission failures remain 401/403 even with continueOnFailure;
processing errors preserve every element outcome.

parameters.name: continueOnFailure
parameters.description:
Continue sequential processing after a failure and suppress the
top-level status for business errors. Does not suppress 401, 403, 429 or 5xx
failures, or permit partial application when atomic=true.

parameters.name: atomic
parameters.description:
Submit all operations as one atomic batch under the optional
Idempotency-Key header. Per-element ik values are ignored.
All elements target ledgerName. On failure every element reports
the batch error; continueOnFailure does not change atomicity.

400.description: Bulk operations completed with errors, or invalid request

429.description:
A per-element error mapped to `KindResourceExhausted` (quota,
rate limit, or authoritative-sequence exhaustion during processing). Surfaces unconditionally,
regardless of `continueOnFailure`. Body carries the per-element
details in `data`.

401.description: Authentication failure before processing or in an element, including a missing mandatory signature (UNAUTHENTICATED); never suppressed by continueOnFailure

403.description: Insufficient scope, mismatched signed batch, or invalid/unknown/revoked signature (PERMISSION_DENIED); never suppressed by continueOnFailure

404.description: A ledger or resource was not found during processing

409.description: An element or the atomic batch conflicts with existing state

503.description:
Retryable processing failure, including leader loss or an expired
admission cache horizon. Surfaces regardless of continueOnFailure.
Inspect per-element outcomes before retrying a non-atomic batch.

Retry-After.description: Number of seconds to wait before retrying

500.description:
Processing failure with per-element outcomes, or an ordinary error
from panic recovery. Surfaces regardless of continueOnFailure.
An infrastructure failure does not establish whether work committed.

`GET /v3/{ledgerName}/indexes/{canonicalId}` first when the caller must
know that it exists. `404` means that the ledger does not exist.

connectors that implement the conversions capability. A conversion
is a direct swap between two assets on a PSP (e.g. USD → USDC on
Coinbase Prime). Conversions are **read-only** through the Formance
API.

Unlike orders, conversions do not carry an adjustment history —
Formance records only the final observed state (`status`,
`destinationAmount`, and `fee` when settled).

Results are cursor-paginated. The optional request body accepts a
query builder for filtering over top-level `V3Conversion` fields
such as `connectorID`, `reference`, `status`, `sourceAsset`,
`destinationAsset`, and `createdAt`.

for the given ID.

BearerAuth.description:
JWT token issued by a trusted OIDC provider. Required when the server is started with `--auth-enabled`. Scopes: `ledger:read` (read operations), `ledger:write` (write operations), `ledger:admin` (cluster operations).
OIDC/JWT bearer token. When `AUTH_ENABLED=true` the token's issuer,
signature, expiry and not-before are validated against `AUTH_ISSUER`, and a scope is
enforced per method:
  - read methods (GET/HEAD) require `connectivity:read` (`connectivity:write` is also accepted),
  - mutating methods (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) require `connectivity:write`.

Authentication and scope failures yield `401 Unauthorized` with no body. `http bearer`
security schemes cannot formally carry scopes in OpenAPI 3.0, so the
required scope is documented on each operation and via the `401`
response rather than in the scheme itself.

ledgerV3_PageToken.description:
Page token of a paged list. Clients normally pass back the `next` or
`previous` value of a previous response verbatim; building one by hand
is supported.

A token is base64url (unpadded, RFC 4648 §5) of the JSON object
`{"key": <string>, "back": <bool>}`. Both fields are omitted when empty,
and unknown fields are rejected. `key` is a position in the endpoint's
textual form:

  - transactions: decimal transaction id
  - logs: decimal ledger-local log id
  - audit entries: decimal audit sequence
  - accounts: address
  - ledgers and numscripts: name
  - signing keys: key id
  - prepared queries: decimal id for TRANSACTIONS and LOGS targets,
    address for ACCOUNTS
  - index inspection: base64url of the encoded metadata value

Both directions exclude the key and return rows in the requested order
(`reverse` included):

  - `{"key": K}` serves the rows strictly after K;
  - `{"key": K, "back": true}` serves the page that ends strictly
    before K;
  - `{"back": true}` serves the last page;
  - an absent or empty token, or `e30` (`{}`), serves the first page.

On a forward page, `next` is set when a further row follows the page,
and `previous` whenever the request carried a key. On a back page,
`previous` is set when a further row precedes the page, and `next`
whenever the request carried a key. A first page therefore has no
`previous`, and the last page requested with `{"back": true}` has no
`next`. A malformed token, or a key that is not a valid position for
the endpoint, is rejected with 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`.

ledgerV3_MetadataValue.description: A typed metadata value (string, integer, boolean, or null). Integer numbers are decoded exactly, including int64 bounds and values beyond 2^53. Integral decimal and exponent spellings are accepted; fractions and out-of-range values are rejected. String values must not contain NUL bytes. A value is limited to 16384 bytes by default; the effective ceiling comes from the cluster policy (`--metadata-max-value-bytes`). Exceeding it returns 400 with reason `METADATA_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` for a new or expired idempotency key. A live retained key with matching content returns its historical outcome; different content returns 409 with reason `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT`. Requests without a key retain the limit error. Fresh policy refusals are audited without business effects; keyed refusals replay while retained, even if the policy is later loosened.

and the bulk result's `data` surfaces the skip context.

/ internal reasons) are rejected at admission. Accepted
reasons per action on this REST endpoint:
  - `CREATE_TRANSACTION` → `TRANSACTION_REFERENCE_CONFLICT`
  - `REVERT_TRANSACTION` → `TRANSACTION_ALREADY_REVERTED`
  - `DELETE_METADATA`    → `METADATA_NOT_FOUND`

(`ACCOUNT_TYPE_ALREADY_EXISTS`) and `REMOVE_ACCOUNT_TYPE`
(`ACCOUNT_TYPE_NOT_FOUND`), but those actions are **gRPC-only**:
the REST bulk endpoint does not accept account-type actions (see
the `action` enum above), so their reasons are not offered here.
Empty (default) preserves the historical fail-on-error
behaviour.

ledgerV3_QueryFilter.description:
Recursive filter expression using the Formance query DSL (aligned with the v2 API). Each node is an object with **exactly one** top-level `$`-prefixed operator key.

Combinators:
- `{"$and": [QueryFilter, ...]}` — all sub-filters must match (non-empty).
- `{"$or":  [QueryFilter, ...]}` — at least one sub-filter matches (non-empty).
- `{"$not": QueryFilter}` — negates a single sub-filter.

Leaf conditions are a single-key operator whose value is a `{ "<field>": <value> }` map with exactly one field:
- `{"$match": {"<field>": <value>}}` — equality; for `address`/`source`/`destination`


  a trailing `:` means prefix match, otherwise exact.

- `{"$gt"|"$gte"|"$lt"|"$lte": {"<field>": <value>}}` — range bound. A closed


  range is expressed as an `$and` of a lower and an upper bound on the same field.

- `{"$exists": {"metadata": "<key>"}}` — the metadata key is present.
- `{"$exists": {"asset": "<assetRef>"}}` — the account has ever held the asset


  (`assetRef` is `BASE` or `BASE/PRECISION`, e.g. `USD/2`). Requires a READY
  `account-asset` index.


Supported fields: `metadata[<key>]`, `address`, `source`, `destination`, `reference`, `reverted` (bool), `ledger`, `id`, `timestamp`, `insertedAt`, `revertedAt`, `logId`, `date`. Not every field applies to every query target; a field that does not apply is rejected. On the numeric built-ins (`id`, `timestamp`, `insertedAt`, `revertedAt`, `logId`, `date`) use `$gt`/`$gte`/`$lt`/`$lte` for ranges; `$match` is an equality (the closed range from the value to itself). On the audit-entries endpoint only, the bare audit fields (`outcome`, `ledger`, `seq`, `proposal_id`, `timestamp`, `log_seq`, `caller_subject`, `order_type`, `idempotency_key`) replace the `ledger`/`timestamp` meanings above: `$match` on any of them, range operators on the numeric ones, no `$param` values. The log-only fields (`logId`, `date`, `ledger`) are valid only when the prepared query targets `LOGS`; they are rejected on `ACCOUNTS` and `TRANSACTIONS` targets.

A value is either a JSON literal or a parameter reference `{"$param": "<name>"}`, resolved at prepared-query execution time. A JSON `null` in value position is rejected. uint64 fields (`id`, `timestamp`, `insertedAt`, `revertedAt`, `logId`, `date`) are carried as decimal strings to stay lossless above 2^53. The date-semantic fields (`timestamp`, `insertedAt`, `revertedAt`, `date`) additionally accept an RFC3339 timestamp string (e.g. `{"$gte":{"date":"2023-11-14T22:13:20Z"}}`), coerced to the same Unix microseconds as the raw form; a value before the Unix epoch (1970-01-01) is rejected.

ledgerV3_PreparedQueryFilterInput.description:
A filter supplied to a prepared-query create/update request, accepted in EITHER of two interchangeable representations that parse to the same filter and are validated against the same per-target rules (EN-1511):

- the structured JSON QueryFilter object (see `QueryFilter`); or
- the textual filter grammar carried as a JSON string, e.g.


  `"metadata[status] == \"active\""`.


`null` represents a match-all query. An empty object and an empty or whitespace-only textual expression are invalid. Responses echo a stored non-null filter in the structured `QueryFilter` form and omit this field for match-all queries.

ledgerV3_ExecutePreparedQueryResponse.description:
Result of executing a prepared query. Exactly one field is set,
discriminated by the request execution `mode` (see
`ExecutePreparedQueryRequest.mode`): `mode=LIST` returns `cursor`,
`mode=AGGREGATE_VOLUMES` returns `aggregateResult`. (The query `target`
— ACCOUNTS, TRANSACTIONS or LOGS — selects the row type inside the
cursor, not which envelope field is set: `accountData`,
`transactionData` or `logData` respectively. LOGS is a usable
prepared-query target: `query.Execute` hydrates `logData` for it.) Both
payloads use the same camelCase encoding as the equivalent non-prepared
endpoints
(header-negotiated monetary amounts, `color` always present on every volume row
including the uncolored bucket).

clientOrderID.description:
Client-assigned ID supplied to the PSP for placement idempotency
(e.g. Coinbase `client_order_id`, Kraken `cl_ord_id`, Binance
`clientOrderId`). Stored for traceability only — Formance does
NOT dedup on this field.

createdAt.description: When the order was created on the PSP.

updatedAt.description: When Formance last observed a state change on the order. Equivalent to the latest adjustment's `createdAt`.

sourceAsset.description:
Asset being spent, in `SYMBOL/precision` form (e.g. `USD/2`,
`BTC/8`). For BUY: the quote currency. For SELL: the base
currency.

destinationAsset.description:
Asset being received, in `SYMBOL/precision` form.
For BUY: the base currency. For SELL: the quote currency.

baseQuantityOrdered.description: Amount of base asset the order was placed for, as an integer at the base asset's precision.

baseQuantityFilled.description: Amount of base asset filled so far, as an integer at the base asset's precision. Null before any fill.

limitPrice.description: Maximum price (for BUY) or minimum price (for SELL) at which the order may execute, in `priceAsset` precision. Required for LIMIT-family order types; null otherwise.

stopPrice.description: Trigger price at which a STOP / STOP_LIMIT order activates, in `priceAsset` precision. Null for non-stop order types.

expiresAt.description: Expiration instant for `GOOD_UNTIL_DATE_TIME` orders. Null for other time-in-force values.

fee.description: Commission charged by the PSP for the order, as an integer in `feeAsset` precision.

feeAsset.description: Currency the fee is denominated in, in `SYMBOL/precision` form. Typically the quote asset.

averageFillPrice.description: Volume-weighted average price across all fills so far, in `priceAsset` precision. Analytics field — may be absent if the PSP does not report it.

quoteAmount.description:
Total amount of quote currency exchanged so far, as reported by
the PSP (e.g. Coinbase `filled_value`), at `quoteAsset`
precision. For BUY: amount spent. For SELL: amount received.

quoteAsset.description: Quote currency with precision (e.g. `USD/2`). Null when the order has no quote-side amounts reported yet.

priceAsset.description:
Currency + precision under which `limitPrice`, `stopPrice`, and
`averageFillPrice` should be interpreted. Separate from
`quoteAsset` because some PSPs return price strings with more
decimal digits than the quote currency's natural precision.

sourceAccountID.description:
Formance account ID of the wallet the source asset was debited
from. Null if the PSP did not return enough information to
resolve it at ingestion time.

destinationAccountID.description: Formance account ID of the wallet the destination asset was credited to. Null if unresolvable.

adjustments.description: Ordered history of state snapshots for this order. The most recent element reflects the current `status`.

error.description: Human-readable error from the PSP (e.g. rejection reason) when `status` is `FAILED`. Null otherwise.

payments_V3Order.description:
A trade order submitted to an exchange-style PSP. Orders are read-only
in the Formance API: they are fetched from the underlying connector.
Status transitions are captured via the `adjustments` array; each
adjustment is a point-in-time snapshot from the PSP.

id.description: Adjustment ID, composed from the order ID plus the state fields that define uniqueness (status, filled quantity, fee). Idempotent — replaying the same observation produces the same ID.

reference.description: PSP reference the adjustment belongs to (equal to the parent order's `reference`).

createdAt.description: When Formance observed this state. Not the PSP's own timestamp — reflects ingestion time.

baseQuantityFilled.description: Base asset filled at this observation, at the base asset's precision.

fee.description: Cumulative fee at this observation, at `feeAsset` precision.

feeAsset.description: Currency the fee is denominated in, in `SYMBOL/precision` form.

raw.description: Untransformed PSP response payload that produced this adjustment. Retained for debugging and replay.

payments_V3OrderAdjustment.description:
Immutable snapshot of an order's state at a single observation.
Formance records one adjustment per distinct state the PSP reports
(status change, fill progress, fee update). Events are emitted
per-adjustment, not per-order — so a single order can produce many
events over its lifetime.

payments_V3OrderDirectionEnum.description: Whether an order buys or sells the base asset.

payments_V3OrderTypeEnum.description:
Exchange order type. Determines which price fields are meaningful on
`V3Order`: LIMIT-family types use `limitPrice`; STOP-family types use
`stopPrice`; TWAP/VWAP are time-weighted execution algorithms.

payments_V3OrderStatusEnum.description:
Lifecycle of an order on the exchange.
`PENDING` — accepted by the exchange, not yet working.
`OPEN` — live on the book, no fills yet.
`PARTIALLY_FILLED` — live on the book, some base quantity filled.
`FILLED` — fully filled, terminal.
`CANCELLED` — cancelled by the user or system, terminal.
`FAILED` — rejected by the exchange, terminal. See `error` for details.
`EXPIRED` — `timeInForce` elapsed before full fill, terminal.

payments_V3TimeInForceEnum.description:
How long an order is valid on the exchange.
`GOOD_UNTIL_CANCELLED` — rests until explicitly cancelled.
`GOOD_UNTIL_DATE_TIME` — rests until `expiresAt`.
`IMMEDIATE_OR_CANCEL` — fill immediately, cancel any unfilled portion.
`FILL_OR_KILL` — fill fully and immediately, or cancel entirely.

reconciliation_Cadence.description:
Deprecated alias of `periodType`. Same members. Use `periodType`; this is
removed at the next API major.

Kept as its own component so regenerated SDKs keep emitting the
`Cadence` type and its constants — dropping it would delete
`CadenceMonthly` and friends from generated clients and break code that
compiles today, even though the wire contract stays compatible.

On requests either key is accepted. If both carry a value and the values
differ the request is rejected with 400 rather than one being chosen
silently; an empty `cadence` counts as unset rather than as a
conflicting value.

On responses the server always emits both keys, mirroring, but neither
is listed in the `Rule` required set. That understates the guarantee on
purpose. A required property with no schema default generates a value
type in Go, which would turn the published `Rule.Cadence *Cadence` and
`GetCadence() *Cadence` into non-pointers and break existing consumers;
optional-without-default reproduces the published pointer signatures.
The default cannot come back, because generators materialize it into
request bodies and that collides with this alias. Both become required
again at the next API major, when `cadence` goes.

Servers before 2.5.0 do not know `periodType` and ignore it, falling
back to `continuous`. Normally that cannot bite you: `periodType`
reaches clients via an SDK regenerated from this spec, which only exists
once 2.5.0 is released. If you need determinism while a fleet is
mid-upgrade, send both keys with equal values — accepted on every
version.

reconciliation_PeriodType.description:
How long a reconciliation period lasts. Scopes each failing fingerprint
into a period so a March break and an April break are distinct,
independently-closable cases.

Omit the key to get `continuous`, a single unbounded period (live
monitoring). There is deliberately no schema-level `default`: SDK
generators materialize defaults into the serialized body, which would
make an omitted key indistinguishable from an explicit one and collide
with the deprecated `cadence` alias. The server owns the default.

This is not how often the rule runs — that is `schedule`, and the two are
independent: an hourly schedule with a `monthly` period type is normal.
The period type determines the `periodID` an alert is filed under:
`monthly` yields `2026-07`.

reconciliation period. There is exactly one Alert per

one unbounded period, so it behaves as one Alert per (ruleID, fingerprint).
The full history of transitions lives in alert_event
(see /alerts/{alertID}/events).

ledgerV3_SigningKeyId.name: Formance-Signing-Key-Id
ledgerV3_SigningKeyId.description:
Signing key ID. Either signing header, even if empty, selects the signed
wrapper under application/json (including MIME parameters). Both headers
are then required exactly once and nonempty. With neither header present,
ordinary unsigned decoding applies. Missing, empty or repeated signing headers
return 400. A non-JSON or missing content type with either header returns
415. JWT authentication and scopes remain independent.

ledgerV3_RequestSignature.name: Formance-Signature
ledgerV3_RequestSignature.description:
Standard-base64 Ed25519 signature over the exact decoded body payload
(serialized protobuf ApplyBatch bytes). Either signing header, even if
empty, selects the signed wrapper under application/json (including MIME
parameters). Both headers are then required exactly once and nonempty.
With neither header present, ordinary unsigned decoding applies. The signature must
decode to 64 bytes. Missing, empty, repeated, invalid-base64 or wrong-length
signatures return 400. A non-JSON or missing content type returns 415.

Render all response Uint256, BigUint and SignedBigInt values as canonical
decimal strings, regardless of business meaning, including posting
amounts, volume input/output and balances. Ordinary integer IDs/counts,
metadata and explicitly string-encoded counters keep their existing
representation. Case-insensitive true, yes, y and 1 enable
this option, matching Ledger v2. Whitespace is not trimmed. Omission and
every other value retain JSON number tokens. This affects only this
response, including nested objects, maps, arrays, transaction/log/cursor
and bulk results. Request decoding is unchanged.

ledgerV3_Consistency.name: X-Consistency
ledgerV3_Consistency.description:
Read consistency. `linearizable` (the default) runs a Raft ReadIndex
barrier and waits for the receiving node to apply up to it. `stale`
serves the read from the receiving node's own store, with no barrier
and no forwarding to the leader, so the answer may lag the leader.
Matching ignores case and surrounding whitespace. An unknown value, or a
repeated or comma-joined header, returns `400 INVALID_REQUEST` on every
`/v3` route, writes included; a valid value has no effect on writes. The
gRPC equivalent is the `x-consistency` request metadata.

ledgerV3_QueryProfile.name: X-Query-Profile
ledgerV3_QueryProfile.description:
Set to any non-empty value to receive the query profile in the
`X-Query-Profile-Result` response header.

The profile reports server-side request timing (how long the server spent
handling the request, broken down into prepare / execute / read-barrier /
deliver phases) plus the query execution plan. Use it to tell a slow
network from a slow server: `serverDurationUs` is the
consumer-independent server cost, and it excludes both the
caller-requested read barrier and response delivery.

Supported on the transactions list, accounts list, aggregated volumes and
prepared-query execution endpoints. The equivalent gRPC opt-in is the
`x-query-profile` request metadata, answered in the
`x-query-profile-result-bin` trailer; `serverDurationUs` has the same
definition on both surfaces, so the two are directly comparable.

ledgerV3_ListFilter.name: filter
ledgerV3_ListFilter.description:
A filter, accepted in EITHER of two interchangeable representations that
parse to the same filter and are validated against the same per-target
rules:

  - **Textual** — the human-readable filter grammar, e.g.
    `metadata[status] == "active"`, `address ^= "users:"`,
    `metadata[a] == "x" and metadata[b] == "y"`. Passed verbatim as the
    query-parameter value (URL-encoded).
  - **Structured** — the JSON QueryFilter DSL (see the `QueryFilter`
    schema: `$and`/`$or`/`$not` + `$match`/`$gt`/`$exists`/…). Passed by
    URL-encoding the JSON object as the query-parameter value.

A condition that is not valid on the endpoint's target (e.g. a
transaction-only condition on the accounts list) is rejected with 400.
This generic filter is AND-combined with any convenience parameters the
endpoint also exposes (e.g. the transactions `startDate`/`endDate`
timestamp range). Selections that used to have dedicated aliases are
expressed through this filter: an account address prefix via
`filter=address ^= "users:"`, a transaction reference via
`filter=reference == "..."` or `filter={"$match":{"reference":"..."}}`
(URL-encoded).

Both representations cover the same fields under the same names:
`metadata[<key>]`, `address`, `source`, `destination`, `reference`,
`reverted`, `ledger`, `id`, `timestamp`, `insertedAt`, `revertedAt`,
`logId`, `date` (e.g. textual `id > 100 and reverted == false` or
structured `{"$and":[{"$gt":{"id":100}},{"$match":{"reverted":false}}]}`).

Date fields accept either an RFC3339 timestamp or raw Unix microseconds,
in both representations: on transactions `timestamp` / `insertedAt` /
`revertedAt` (e.g. textual `filter=timestamp >= "2023-11-14T22:13:20Z"`
or structured `filter={"$gte":{"timestamp":"2023-11-14T22:13:20Z"}}`), and
on logs `date` (e.g. `filter=date >= "2023-11-14T22:13:20Z"`). An RFC3339
value before the Unix epoch (1970-01-01) is rejected with 400.

Note: the bare audit fields (`outcome`, `ledger`, `seq`, `proposal_id`,
`timestamp`, `log_seq`, `caller_subject`, `order_type`,
`idempotency_key`) are valid only on the audit-entries endpoint, where
both representations resolve them against the audit target.

connectivity_ConnectorVersionName.name: version
connectivity_ConnectorVersionName.description:
Version string of a ConnectorVersion (e.g. `v1.4.2`), or one of the
reserved aliases -- never valid semver, so they cannot collide:
`latest` (the newest Validated version across all channels) or
`stable`/`rc`/`beta`/`alpha` (that channel's head, resolved with
exactly the rules installation uses). An empty channel answers
`404 channel_empty` naming the newest Validated version.

connectivity_Query.name: query
connectivity_Query.description:
JSON-encoded filter in the go-libs query dialect: boolean nodes
`$and`/`$or`/`$not` over leaves `$match`/`$in`/`$exists`/`$like`/
`$gt`/`$gte`/`$lt`/`$lte`, each leaf `{"$op": {"key": value}}`.
The filterable keys, their operators and value enums are exactly the
ones served by `GET /_query/capabilities` for the queried resource;
anything else is rejected with `400 invalid_query`. `$like` uses SQL
wildcards (`%`, `_`). Beware negation over absent fields: `$not` on a
`$match` also selects objects where the key is absent -- conjoin with
`$exists` when that matters.
Examples by collection: `/connectors` accepts `{"$match":{"catalog":"ee"}}`;
`/connectors/{name}/versions` accepts `{"$match":{"version":"v1.0.0"}}`;
`/connections` accepts `{"$match":{"connector":"bitcoin"}}`.

ledgerV3_QueryProfileResult.description:
Query profile for this request, returned only when the request carried the
`X-Query-Profile` header. The value is the base64 (standard alphabet)
encoding of a serialized `QueryProfile` protobuf message
(`misc/proto/bucket.proto`).

Key durations, all in microseconds:

  - `serverDurationUs` — consumer-independent server cost: request entry
    to response-ready, excluding the read barrier and response delivery.
    Cannot be moved by a slow client. Over HTTP, request entry is the
    router chain just before authentication; over gRPC it is the
    handler's first statement, because grpc-go unmarshals the request
    before dispatching. It does NOT include row serialization.
  - `prepareDurationUs` — authentication, query/body decoding, validation
    and filter compilation.
  - `executeDurationUs` — query execution (contains
    `indexDurationUs` + `enrichmentDurationUs`).
  - `barrierDurationUs` — time blocked on caller-requested read
    consistency waits. Excluded from `serverDurationUs`. Measures LOCAL
    waits only, and counts one that fails or is superseded: see
    `forwarded`.
  - `deliverDurationUs` — response serialization and transport hand-off.
    Excluded from `serverDurationUs`. Always 0 over HTTP: this header
    must be flushed before the response body, so the body write is out
    of reach. It is populated for gRPC server streams.
  - `firstRowDurationUs` — always 0 over HTTP (the response is
    buffered); populated for gRPC server streams.
  - `forwarded` — true when another node served the read. Its barrier and
    execution are then folded into `executeDurationUs`, so the breakdown
    describes the local hop only. `barrierDurationUs` then covers the
    local waits only: 0 means none happened (not "no barrier was
    needed"), non-zero means a `ReadIndex` attempt failed and caused
    the forward. Do not infer the remote node's health from it.

For a latency objective, pick a total and state which: `serverDurationUs`
is client-independent but omits serialization, while
`serverDurationUs + deliverDurationUs` is the complete server-side cost
but absorbs consumer back-pressure on a gRPC stream. Neither is unbiased
on a streaming read.
